# M7.10 Callable and Procedural Execution Contract

This contract is the shared boundary for the M7.10 workstreams. It deliberately
uses the native syntax, semantic, type, and constant-value representations.
Slang is a test oracle only.

## Existing representation and narrow parser additions

- `VerilogCallableDeclaration` owns callable kind, lifetime, return type and
  dimensions, ordered `formal_arguments`, local declarations, body, and
  source location. `VerilogSemanticSymbol` represents each callable; its
  `member_scope` owns local/formal symbols and `callable->formal_arguments`
  preserves formal order and direction/type/dimensions.
- Calls are `VerilogExpressionKind::Call`: `first` is the callee and
  `operands` are actual expressions. The parser workstream adds a parallel
  `operand_names` vector of optional names (same length as `operands`; empty
  name means positional) and parses `.formal(expression)` call syntax.
- The parser workstream adds `VerilogStatementKind::Return`, with its optional
  expression in `VerilogStatement::expression`. A function return is either
  an explicit return expression or the final value assigned to the function
  name. A task may return without a value. A function may not return without a
  value unless it has assigned its function-name variable.
- Existing expression and statement nodes remain owned and preserve source
  locations. No second expression, statement, type, or symbol representation
  is introduced.

## Binding and compatibility

`bind_verilog_callable_arguments()` in the binding workstream consumes the
resolved callable symbol, call expression, and existing type-analysis result.
It returns ordered `(formal symbol, optional actual expression)` bindings and
source-located diagnostics.

The public binding result contains `arguments` (each with
`formal_index`, `formal`, and nullable `actual`), `diagnostics` using a
binding diagnostic with `VerilogTypeDiagnosticSeverity`, code/message,
source location, and optional related formal location, plus `is_valid`.
Binding entry points are:

```cpp
VerilogCallableBindingResult bind_verilog_callable_arguments(
    const VerilogSemanticSymbol& callable, const VerilogExpression& call,
    const VerilogTypeAnalysisResult& type_analysis);

const VerilogCallableDeclaration* find_verilog_callable_declaration(
    const VerilogCompilationUnit& syntax, const VerilogSemanticSymbol& callable);
```

- A call uses either all positional or all named actuals; mixed calls are
  invalid. Positional actuals bind in declaration order. Named actuals bind
  by exact formal name; duplicates, unknown names, and missing formals are
  errors. Every formal is required; defaults and empty/unconnected subroutine
  actuals are unsupported.
- Function formals must be `input`. Tasks support input, output, inout, and
  ref. Output/inout/ref require assignable actuals. The initial execution
  subset propagates output values only to simple identifier actuals; other
  lvalue forms are diagnosed as unsupported by execution.
- Known integral input/output/inout width and signedness conversions are
  warnings, consistent with ordinary assignment conversion. `ref` requires
  matching known category, width, signedness, and four-state status. Unknown
types remain unknown and are not coerced. For named enum/aggregate types,
`ref` also requires the same resolved type identity and matching packed and
unpacked dimensions.

## Execution

The shared `VerilogCallableExecutionState` carries the immutable options,
global statement-step count, active callable-symbol stack, and diagnostics.
Default limits are 100,000 executed statements and call depth 64. Recursive
re-entry is diagnosed separately from depth exhaustion. Limits are shared by
nested function/task calls. A failed operation returns diagnostics; it never
silently substitutes a value.

- `VerilogConstantEnvironment` is the execution frame: it maps visible
  parameter/global/local/formal names to independent four-state constant
  values. Each invocation gets a fresh frame; input actuals are evaluated in
  the caller frame, then copied into formal names. Inout/ref actuals are also
  copied in; output formals begin at their type's default uninitialized value.
  Local declarations use
  their initializer when present; otherwise 4-state integral locals start X
  and 2-state integral locals start zero. Function return values use the
  declared return width/signedness through existing type information.
- Expressions are evaluated by `evaluate_verilog_constant()` and its existing
  resolver. User function calls in expressions recurse through the native
  function evaluator. Other unsupported expressions produce diagnostics.
- Supported statements are sequential blocks, blocking assignments,
  conditionals, case/casez/casex, bounded for/while/repeat/forever loops,
  null statements, explicit return, and nested task calls. Conditions and
  case matching require fully known integral values. Nonblocking assignments,
  timing/event controls, wait, unsupported statements, and unsupported
  lvalue writeback are diagnosed; they are not simulated or ignored.
- Functions execute in a private frame and do not mutate caller variables.
  Their result is the explicit return expression or function-name variable.
  Tasks execute in a private frame, then write output/inout/ref formal values
  back to their bound simple identifier actuals only after successful return.
  Inout/ref initial values are copied into the callee frame before execution.
- Execution is synchronous and deterministic. It does not model event
  scheduling, delays, simulator time, four-state procedural branch merging,
  or global side effects.

Public execution entry points have these signatures:

```cpp
VerilogFunctionEvaluationResult evaluate_verilog_function_call(
    const VerilogCompilationUnit& syntax,
    const VerilogSemanticAnalysisResult& semantic,
    const VerilogTypeAnalysisResult& type_analysis,
    const VerilogExpression& call,
    const VerilogConstantEnvironment& caller_environment = {},
    VerilogCallableExecutionOptions options = {});

VerilogTaskExecutionResult execute_verilog_task_call(
    const VerilogCompilationUnit& syntax,
    const VerilogSemanticAnalysisResult& semantic,
    const VerilogTypeAnalysisResult& type_analysis,
    const VerilogExpression& call,
    VerilogConstantEnvironment& caller_environment,
    VerilogCallableExecutionOptions options = {});
```

Each also has an overload replacing `options` with a shared
`VerilogCallableExecutionState&` for nested execution. Function results expose
an optional constant `value`, diagnostics, and executed step count; task
results expose `completed`, diagnostics, and step count. The task environment
is passed by non-const reference and is updated only on successful completion.

## File ownership for this milestone

| Workstream | Exclusive write ownership |
|---|---|
| A. Legacy ports and parser AST additions | `include/labneura/eda/verilog_syntax.h`, `src/labneura/eda/verilog_syntax.cpp`, `tests/eda_verilog_legacy_ports_test.cpp` |
| B. Callable binding and compatibility | `include/labneura/eda/verilog_callable_binding.h`, `src/labneura/eda/verilog_callable_binding.cpp`, `tests/eda_verilog_callable_binding_test.cpp` |
| C. Function evaluation | `include/labneura/eda/verilog_function_evaluation.h`, `src/labneura/eda/verilog_function_evaluation.cpp`, `tests/eda_verilog_function_evaluation_test.cpp` |
| D. Task execution | `include/labneura/eda/verilog_task_execution.h`, `src/labneura/eda/verilog_task_execution.cpp`, `tests/eda_verilog_task_execution_test.cpp` |
| Integration lead | This contract, `include/labneura/eda/verilog_callable_execution.h`, `CMakeLists.txt`, existing semantic/type integration, and frontend/current-state documentation |

Agents may read other files but must not edit outside their exact ownership.
Any required shared contract or AST change must be requested before
implementation; only the integration lead may change CMake and existing
semantic/type integration files.
